I first began thinking about this while studying cardiac troponin, the biomarker used in
emergency care to help diagnose a heart attack. The paradox is that it also rises in healthy
athletes after a race or a match. The same molecule. The same increase. And two incompatible
meanings.

I devoted my doctoral thesis to understanding this paradox. But what I really took from it
was a question that still guides everything I do: how do we measure what exercise does to
the body, why do we measure it that way, and, above all, what can we claim from what we have
measured?
